extracted.intended_audience: aspiring authors and writers who want to participate in Twitter pitch events to reach agents/publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting single-tweet pitches during Twitter pitch events to attract literary agents or publishers, including how to craft the pitch, prepare manuscripts, follow event rules, and engage professionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tweet format and hashtag requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each pitch must fit inside a single tweet, and include the event’s unique hashtags so agents and publishers can easily find your submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitch events usually require your pitch to be under Twitter's character limit (fewer than 280 characters) and to use the event hashtag(s). Events often have additional hashtags for theme, subject, age group, or genre — include those or agents may not see your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research the event and target audience/agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you know as much about the pitch event as possible: read the guidelines carefully and understand the rules and requirements to ensure you’re targeting the right audience and the right agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the format, length, any special prompts or additional hashtags, and who the participating agents/editors are. Visit the event website and check event-specific rules so you position your pitch appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft a concise, attention-grabbing pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: Your pitch should be concise, attention-grabbing, and accurately reflect the essence of your story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid plot-specific language; stick to generalities so the pitch is easy to understand. Make the stakes clear and don’t be vague. Use a character’s distinctive skill/trait to sell the story. Avoid rhetorical questions. Write several drafts and get feedback from friends or writing groups before posting. Use practice pitch events (e.g., #PracPit) to refine your pitch. Treat the brevity requirement as practice for query letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript must be submission-ready (fiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless you’re participating in a non-fiction pitch event, make sure your manuscript is in the best shape possible and ready to hand to an agent the second they request it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your manuscript should be complete, revised, edited, and have feedback from beta readers so it’s as close to publishing standard as possible. For traditional-publishing-oriented pitches you typically don’t need to hire an editor as you would for self-publishing, but it must be polished and ready to submit quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active participation and engagement etiquette
rubrics_metrics.description: Be active on Twitter during the event and engage with others who are participating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retweet and comment where encouraged to amplify voices and network. Many pitch events rely on agents being the only ones to 'like' a pitch as an expression of interest, so avoid liking other writers’ pitches unless the event explicitly allows it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow up with interested agents/publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: After the event, follow up with any agents or publishers who express interest to build relationships and provide more information as requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the event, make a list of agents/publishers who liked or retweeted your pitch and note any specific comments or feedback. Reach out afterwards to thank them, provide requested materials, and continue the conversation to increase chances of representation or a deal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose appropriate, genre- or mission-specific events
rubrics_metrics.description: Many pitch events are genre-specific or focused on particular communities, and each has its own rules and aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select events that match your work (e.g., #DVPit for marginalized voices, #HarlequinPitch for romance, #SFFPit for science fiction and fantasy). Check each event’s website for rules and positioning advice. Note that some events (e.g., #PitLight) may not include agents, so pick events aligned with your goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pitch events as practice and networking opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if you don’t secure representation immediately, pitch events are valuable for exposure, networking, and practicing concise pitching skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat events as low-risk practice for query letters and a way to gauge audience response. Engage with the wider writing community to gain insight and connections that can help your publishing journey.
